info.headline: Catch the key words you hear.
info.summary: Level A is for students who are just starting to learn English. You will hear one to three short, slow sentences about your classroom, math, science, and stories. Pictures and emoji help you understand. You listen for key words like names, numbers, places, and feelings, and then choose the answer that matches.
canDo: I can follow a short classroom direction.
I can find a place or thing when I hear its name and a place word.
I can catch numbers and math words like "in all" and "more."
I can put two or three story events in order with first, next, and then.

activities.title: Where Does the Book Go?
activities.skill: Following a one-step classroom direction with place words
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the classroom. Listen to your teacher. Then choose the place the teacher talks about.
activities.prompt: Where does the teacher want you to put the book?

picture.alt: A classroom with a window and a bookshelf under it, a whiteboard, a teacher's desk, cubbies by the door, and a round reading rug on the floor.

activities.script: Please put your book on the shelf. The shelf is under the window.

options.text: On the shelf under the window
In the cubby by the door with the coats

vocabulary: a flat board where we keep books and things
estante: tabla plana donde guardamos libros y cosas
debajo de: más abajo que otra cosa
glass in the wall that lets light in
ventana: vidrio en la pared que deja entrar la luz
activities.correct: Yes! You heard "shelf" and "under the window." Two clues helped you find the place.
activities.hint: Listen for the name of a thing in the room. Then listen for a place word like "under."
activities.support: Point to the window in the picture. Now look below it. What do you see there?
activities.extension: Tell a partner where to put a pencil. Use a place word: on, under, or next to.
wida: Inform: identify a place from a spoken direction

teacher.use: Use in the first weeks for newcomers learning classroom routines and place words.
teacher.function: Follow a one-step oral direction; locate objects with place words.
teacher.lower: Read twice and point to the window while you say it. Accept pointing as the answer.
teacher.onLevel: Read once at a slow, clear pace.
teacher.challenge: Give a two-step direction: put the book on the shelf, then sit on the rug.
teacher.noTech: Print the classroom picture. Students place a paper book cut-out where you say.
teacher.prompt: Which two words helped you find the place?

activities.title: What Do You Need for Math?
activities.skill: Listening for needed items in a direction
activities.directions: Listen to your teacher. Choose ALL the things you need. There is more than one answer.
activities.prompt: What do you need for math today?
activities.script: For math today, you need a pencil and a ruler. You do not need crayons.
vocabulary: a tool to measure how long something is
regla: herramienta para medir qué tan largo es algo
no: palabras que dicen que algo no pasa
activities.correct: Great listening! You need a pencil and a ruler. You also caught "do not need crayons."
activities.hint: Listen for "you need." Then listen for "do not need." Those words tell you what to leave.
activities.support: Hold up a pencil and a ruler. Say: I need a pencil. I need a ruler. I do not need crayons.
activities.extension: Tell a partner two things you need for reading time.
wida: Inform: identify items named in a direction

teacher.use: Morning routine or math launch for Level 1 students.
teacher.function: Identify items named in an oral direction; notice negation.
teacher.lower: Show real supplies on the table. Students touch each one as you say it.
teacher.onLevel: Read once; students choose both items.
teacher.challenge: Add a third item and a second "do not" to track.
teacher.noTech: Students hold up the real supplies they hear.
teacher.prompt: What word told you NOT to take something?

activities.title: Find Amir on the Playground
activities.skill: Locating a person with place words
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the playground. Listen. Then choose where Amir is.
activities.prompt: Where is Amir?

picture.alt: A playground with a slide, swings, a big tree, and a bench. A child plays at each place.

activities.script: This is my friend Amir. He is under the big tree. He likes the shade.

options.text: On the slide near the tall fence

vocabulary: debajo de: más abajo que otra cosa
a tall plant with a trunk and leaves
árbol: planta alta con tronco y hojas
a cool, dark place out of the sun
sombra: lugar fresco donde no llega el sol
activities.correct: Yes! Amir is under the big tree. The word "shade" was another clue: trees make shade.
activities.hint: Listen for a place word: on, under, or next to. Then listen for the thing.
activities.support: Point to each place in the picture and say its name with your teacher: slide, swings, tree, bench.
activities.extension: Choose another child in the picture. Tell a partner where that child is.
wida: Inform: locate a person using place words

teacher.use: Use with the playground picture to practice place words and recess vocabulary.
teacher.function: Locate a person or object from an oral description.
teacher.lower: Read twice. Point to the tree while saying "under the big tree."
teacher.onLevel: Read once at a slow pace.
teacher.challenge: Students describe where another child is; a partner points.
teacher.noTech: Print the picture; students put a counter on the place they hear.
teacher.prompt: What place word did you hear?

activities.title: Which Circle Did You Hear?
activities.skill: Matching a spoken fraction description to a model
activities.directions: Listen to your teacher describe a circle. Choose the matching circle.
activities.prompt: Which picture shows the circle the teacher describes?
activities.script: This circle has four equal parts. Three parts are shaded.

picture.alt: A circle cut into four equal parts. One part is shaded.
A circle cut into six equal parts. Three parts are shaded.
A circle cut into four equal parts. Two parts are shaded.
A circle cut into four equal parts. Three parts are shaded.

vocabulary: pieces that are all the same size
partes iguales: pedazos que tienen el mismo tamaño
a number that names part of a whole
fracción: número que nombra una parte de un entero
frames: ___ parts are shaded. That is three fourths.
activities.correct: Yes! Four equal parts and three are shaded. That is the fraction three fourths.
activities.hint: You need TWO numbers: how many parts in all, and how many are shaded.
activities.support: Count with your finger: how many parts in each circle? Find the circles with 4 parts first.
activities.extension: Draw a circle with four equal parts. Shade one part. Tell a partner: One part is shaded.
wida: Inform: match a description to a math model
Language of Math: equal parts, shaded

teacher.use: Grade 3 fractions: connect spoken fraction language to area models.
teacher.function: Process two quantities in an oral description to identify a model.
teacher.lower: Read twice. Hold up four fingers, then three, as you read.
teacher.onLevel: Read once; ask students to say the fraction name after answering.
teacher.challenge: Students describe a circle for a partner to draw.
teacher.noTech: Draw the four circles on the board; students point.
teacher.prompt: Why is Circle 2 not the answer, even with three shaded parts?

activities.title: The Part That Drinks Water

activities.directions: Look at the picture of the plant. Listen to the clue. Choose the plant part.
activities.prompt: Which part of the plant is the teacher talking about?

activities.script: This part of the plant is under the ground. It takes in water from the soil.
vocabulary: plant parts under the ground that take in water
raíces: partes de la planta bajo la tierra que toman agua
suelo: tierra donde crecen las plantas
activities.correct: Correct! The roots are under the ground and take in water from the soil.
activities.hint: Listen for WHERE the part is: "under the ground." Look at the bottom of the picture.
activities.support: Point to each part in the picture with your teacher: flower, leaves, stem, roots.
activities.extension: Choose another part. Tell its job: The leaves ___.
wida: Inform: identify a plant part from its location and job

teacher.function: Identify a part from a spoken description of location and function.
teacher.lower: Read twice; trace the line from the soil to the roots.
teacher.onLevel: Read once.

teacher.noTech: Bring a real plant with roots showing; students point.

activities.title: What Is the Weather?

activities.support: Act it out: shiver for cold, wave your arms for wind. Which symbol matches?
activities.extension: Tell a partner what to wear on a rainy day.

activities.title: Lucía's Morning
activities.skill: Putting three spoken steps in order
activities.directions: Listen to Lucía's morning at school. Put the steps in order.
activities.prompt: What does Lucía do first, next, and then?
activities.script: First, Lucía hangs up her backpack. Next, she eats breakfast. Then, she reads a book.
vocabulary: primero: antes que todos los demás
a bag you carry on your back
mochila: bolsa que llevas en la espalda
activities.correct: Great! First the backpack, next breakfast, then a book. Order words helped you.
activities.hint: Listen for first, next, and then. Each one starts a new step.
activities.support: Hold up one finger for first, two for next, three for then while you listen again.
activities.extension: Tell your own morning with first, next, and then.
wida: Narrate: retell events in order using first, next, then

teacher.use: Use to teach sequence words with a familiar school routine.
teacher.function: Sequence events in a short oral narrative.
teacher.lower: Read twice; students hold up fingers for each step.
teacher.onLevel: Read once.

teacher.prompt: Which word told you the last step?

activities.title: How Many Apples?
activities.skill: Listening for numbers in a math story
activities.directions: Listen to the math story. Choose the numbers you hear.
activities.prompt: Fill in the numbers from Kofi's story.
activities.script: Kofi has 5 red apples. He has 3 green apples. He has 8 apples in all.
vocabulary: the total when you put groups together
en total: lo que hay al juntar los grupos
activities.correct: Yes! 5 red and 3 green make 8 in all. 5 + 3 = 8.
activities.hint: Listen for the color word, then the number before it.
activities.support: Use counters: put out 5 red and 3 green. Count them all together.
activities.extension: Make your own story: ___ has ___ cats and ___ dogs. How many in all?
wida: Inform: identify numbers in an oral math story

teacher.use: Math warm-up for addition language.
teacher.function: Process numbers and the phrase "in all" in an oral word problem.
teacher.lower: Read twice slowly; hold up fingers for each number.
teacher.onLevel: Read once.
teacher.challenge: Change to a subtraction story: Kofi ate 2. How many are left?
teacher.noTech: Students use cubes to build the story as you read.
teacher.prompt: What does "in all" mean?

activities.title: Water or Land?
activities.skill: Sorting animals by habitat from an oral description
activities.directions: Listen to your teacher. Sort each animal: does it live in water or on land?
activities.prompt: Where does each animal live?
activities.script: A fish, a whale, and an octopus live in the water. A cow, a horse, and a rabbit live on land.
vocabulary: to have a home in a place
vivir: tener casa en un lugar
tierra: el suelo, no el agua
activities.correct: Nice sorting! Fish, whales, and octopuses live in water. Cows, horses, and rabbits live on land.
activities.hint: The teacher says three animals, then where they live. Listen for "in the water" and "on land."
activities.support: Make two piles with your hands: water on one side, land on the other. Move each animal as you hear it.
activities.extension: Name one more animal. Does it live in water or on land?
wida: Inform: classify animals from spoken information

teacher.use: Science: animal habitats.
teacher.function: Classify information heard in an oral description.
teacher.lower: Read one sentence at a time; sort after each sentence.
teacher.onLevel: Read both sentences, then sort.
teacher.challenge: Ask about a frog: Where does it live? (both — a good talk question).
teacher.noTech: Use animal picture cards and two hoops on the floor.
teacher.prompt: Which animal was the hardest? Why?

activities.title: Mei's Mitten

activities.title: Who Read More?

activities.directions: Listen to two students talk about reading. Choose the answer.

páginas: las hojas de un libro
look at how things are the same or different

activities.hint: Listen for each name and the number after it. Then compare the two numbers.

activities.extension: How many more pages did Amara read? (20 − 12 = ?)

activities.title: Busy Bees: The Main Idea
activities.skill: Identifying the main idea of a science mini-lecture
activities.directions: Listen to a short science talk about bees and flowers. Then choose the main idea of the whole talk.
activities.prompt: What is the main idea of the talk?
activities.script: Have you ever watched a bee visit a flower? The bee is looking for food. Flowers make a sweet liquid called nectar, and bees drink it. While the bee drinks, a yellow powder called pollen sticks to its fuzzy body. When the bee flies to the next flower, some of that pollen rubs off. Moving pollen from flower to flower is called pollination. Pollination helps plants make seeds, so new plants can grow. Without bees and other pollinators, many fruits and vegetables could not grow.

options.text: Bees drink nectar because it is sweet.
Some fruits are sweeter than others, so bees come to the sweetest flowers first.
Bees help plants make seeds by carrying pollen from flower to flower.

listenFor: the topic in the first sentences

activities.hint: A main idea covers the WHOLE talk. A detail is only one small part. Which answer connects most of the sentences?
activities.support: Ask yourself: Why did the speaker tell me about nectar and pollen? What were all those details building to?
activities.extension: Explain why farmers might care about bees. Use the word pollination.

activities.title: Nia's Plant Test
activities.skill: Drawing a conclusion from an investigation
activities.directions: Listen to a student report on a plant investigation. Then choose the best conclusion.
activities.prompt: What can Nia conclude from her investigation?
activities.script: Nia tested what plants need. She planted two bean plants of the same size in the same kind of soil. She gave both plants the same amount of water. She put Plant A on a sunny window shelf and Plant B in a dark closet. After two weeks, Plant A had grown six centimeters and had green leaves. Plant B had grown only one centimeter, and its leaves were pale yellow.

options.text: Plant B needed more water than Plant A.
Bean plants need light to grow well.
Bean plants grow better with less water.
Dark closets make soil lose its nutrients.

activities.directions: Listen to the talk about the five senses. Choose ALL the sentences that match what the speaker says.

activities.prompt: Why is the nurse calling families?
activities.script: Hello, this is Ms. Okafor, the school nurse. I am calling about Tuesday.
